alternatives.concept: Combine economic theory and empirical analysis with law, political institutions and public policy. Mathematical/statistical foundations, money/trade and contemporary economic applications support decisions about markets, government and welfare.

alternatives.labelRationale: The completed program combines actual economics and empirical foundations with behavioral/social explanation and inequality, without claiming a full Leiden degree or named formal route.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest, replaces banking/trade/AI and EU-political emphasis with sustained sociological/psychological explanation, original survey work and social opportunity. Five actual changes implement that priority; economics is retained.

alternatives.concept: Retain economic theory, quantitative evidence and institutions while concentrating on climate impacts, life-cycle assessment, environmental justice and collective sustainability decisions. These approaches complement economic policy analysis; they do not reproduce Leiden’s integrated climate-economic model.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest, four substantive changes replace financial/trade/AI/EU-political emphasis with climate science, life-cycle impacts/costs, environmental justice and sustainability governance. Compared with the behavioral program, different environmental objects and policy-evaluation methods organize the work. No arbitrary threshold repair.

audience.programmeDescription: Economics & Society at Leiden combines economic theory and empirical analysis with law, politics and institutions. Students examine welfare, inequality, climate change, migration and labour markets, and learn to assess economic policy and its social consequences. The programme is taught in The Hague in cooperation with Erasmus School of Economics. Tutoring supports academic and career development.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified academic-core comparison assesses the confirmed first 120 EC with Package A. Three UCR programs combine economic theory and empirical analysis with institutions, behavior and inequality, or climate governance. All 180 EC of the published outline remain visible, but the final 30 required EC and project are shown only at outline level and are outside the academic comparison. Dutch fiscal/social law, specialist labour/migration study, integrated climate-economic modelling and some causal methods remain differences.

curriculum.limitation: The published outline totals 180 EC, including 30 EC of elective space and a 10-EC bachelor project. Detailed third-year, cohort and project requirements remain unconfirmed. This is an indicative programme outline, not a certified complete degree pathway.
